extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers in differential equations / mathematical biology (advanced undergraduates and graduate students)
extracted.subtask_description: Qualitative modeling and phase-plane analysis of population dynamics: SIR / SIRS epidemic models, predator–prey (Volterra–Lotka) systems with and without limited growth, and general two-species competition models. The page states modeling assumptions, equilibrium conditions, nullcline/phase-portrait analysis, invariance arguments, Lyapunov functions, and consequences (stability, limit cycles, long-term behavior).

rubrics_metrics.name: SIR model assumptions and equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide population into susceptible S, infected I, recovered R; total population constant (S+I+R constant). Assume no reinfection, transmission rate proportional to encounters, and recovery rate proportional to infected. Model: S' = -β S I, I' = β S I - ν I, R' = ν I with β, ν > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These assumptions justify reducing the dynamics to the two-dimensional system in S and I because S+I+R is constant. The proportional-to-encounters assumption is expressed by a bilinear contact term βSI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to two-dimensional S–I system
rubrics_metrics.description: With total population constant, determine S(t) and I(t); R(t) follows by conservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It suffices to analyze the planar system S' = -βSI, I' = βSI - νI; phase-plane analysis of this reduced system provides full population dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIR equilibrium linearization criterion (threshold S = ν/β)
rubrics_metrics.description: Linearization at (S,0) gives eigenvalues 0 and βS - ν. The second eigenvalue is negative if 0 < S < ν/β and positive if S > ν/β.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus S = ν/β is a threshold dividing parameter/initial-condition regimes where small infections decay or grow; used to infer local behavior along the S-axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIR nullclines and qualitative phase behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: S-nullclines are the S- and I-axes; I-nullclines are I=0 and the vertical line S = ν/β. For initial data with S0 > ν/β and I0 > 0, S decreases monotonically and I initially rises then declines to 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nullcline diagram and direction field to infer monotonicity and transient peaks of infected population; nullcline crossings determine vector directions in regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conserved quantity for SIR (first integral)
rubrics_metrics.description: The function I + S - (ν/β) log S is constant along solution curves; equivalently solutions satisfy I = -S + (ν/β) log S + constant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This first integral allows analytic description of solution curves and shows unique connecting trajectories between equilibria across the threshold S = ν/β.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIRS model: reinfection and equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow recovered individuals to lose immunity and reenter susceptibles at rate µ: S' = -β S I + µ R, I' = β S I - ν I, R' = ν I - µ R, with β, µ, ν, τ (>0) and total population S+I+R = τ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate R using R = τ - S - I to obtain a planar system; parameters µ and τ introduce new equilibria and threshold behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIRS threshold and bifurcation condition (τ ≥ ν/β)
rubrics_metrics.description: The second (endemic) equilibrium exists only when total population τ ≥ ν/β. When τ = ν/β the two equilibria coalesce (bifurcation). The quantity ν/β is called the threshold level for the disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: disease can become established only when total population exceeds threshold; this is a parameter-dependent bifurcation criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local stability at disease-free SIRS equilibrium
rubrics_metrics.description: At (τ,0) the linearization has eigenvalues -µ and βτ - ν; this equilibrium is a saddle if βτ - ν > 0 (i.e., τ > ν/β).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the signs of eigenvalues from linearization to classify local behavior (saddle vs. stable) at the disease-free equilibrium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability of endemic SIRS equilibrium via trace/determinant
rubrics_metrics.description: At the endemic equilibrium (when it exists) the linearization has negative trace and positive determinant, hence eigenvalues with negative real parts and the point is asymptotically stable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply standard linearization criteria (trace < 0, determinant > 0) to conclude asymptotic stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive invariance of triangular region for SIRS
rubrics_metrics.description: Region Δ defined by S, I ≥ 0 and S + I ≤ τ is positively invariant: vector field points inward or tangent along each boundary segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check vector field directions along boundary segments (I=0, S=0, hypotenuse S+I=τ) to show solutions starting in Δ remain in Δ; useful to restrict global dynamics to biologically relevant domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volterra–Lotka predator–prey model assumptions and equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Prey x grows at rate ax in absence of predators, predators y decline at rate -cy in absence of prey. Predation terms assumed proportional to encounters giving x' = x(a - b y), y' = y(-c + d x), with a,b,c,d > 0 and x,y ≥ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These ecological assumptions (exponential growth/decay and bilinear interaction) define the classic Lotka–Volterra system used for phase-plane analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equilibria and linearization for Volterra–Lotka
rubrics_metrics.description: Equilibria at (0,0) and Z = (c/d, a/b). Linearization at origin yields eigenvalues a and -c (a saddle). At Z the eigenvalues are pure imaginary ± i sqrt(ac) (linearization inconclusive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local linearization to identify saddle behavior at origin; interior point requires nonlinear analysis (e.g., conserved quantity or Lyapunov function) to determine nature of orbits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nullclines and rotational direction for Volterra–Lotka
rubrics_metrics.description: x-nullclines: x=0 and y=a/b; y-nullclines: y=0 and x=c/d. Nonzero nullclines partition positive quadrant into four regions; solutions wind counterclockwise about interior equilibrium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nullcline geometry to deduce direction of flow in each region and qualitative rotation around Z.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of first integral / Lyapunov-like function for Volterra–Lotka
rubrics_metrics.description: The function L(x,y) = d x - c log x + b y - a log y is constant along solution curves (˙L ≡ 0) for x,y > 0 and has an absolute minimum at Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This conserved quantity implies closed orbits (level sets of L) and shows Z is a (non-asymptotically) stable center in the classical system; it is used to rule out limit cycles and to classify solution behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global behavior for classical predator–prey (closed orbits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every solution of the classical Volterra–Lotka system (except those on coordinate axes or at the equilibrium Z) lies on a closed orbit; populations oscillate cyclically and neither species goes extinct nor grows without bound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine first integral, absence of limit cycles, and phase portrait to conclude all interior orbits are periodic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predator–prey with limited growth (logistic terms) and nullclines L and M
rubrics_metrics.description: Include logistic self-limitation: x' = x(a - b y - λ x), y' = y(-c + d x - µ y) with λ,µ > 0. Nullclines: L: a - b y - λ x = 0, M: -c + d x - µ y = 0. Behavior depends on whether L and M intersect in Q = {x,y>0}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If L and M don't intersect in Q one outcome occurs (predator extinction); if they intersect at Z, Z is an interior equilibrium whose stability can be analyzed by trace/determinant and Poincaré–Bendixson.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome when limited-growth nullclines do not intersect
rubrics_metrics.description: If L and M do not meet in Q, all solutions in the positive quadrant tend to the prey-only equilibrium (a/λ, 0) and predators become extinct; prey approaches carrying capacity a/λ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nullcline geometry combined with monotonicity arguments shows trajectories either meet L or tend to (a/λ,0); crossing properties prevent return to predator persistence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interior equilibrium and global alternatives via Poincaré–Bendixson
rubrics_metrics.description: When L and M intersect at Z in Q, Z has trace < 0 and determinant > 0 (hence asymptotically stable). Invariant rectangles exist; by Poincaré–Bendixson the ω-limit set of any interior point is either Z or a limit cycle surrounding Z. Populations thus approach a constant or periodic solution and remain bounded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct positively invariant rectangles to confine dynamics; use Poincaré–Bendixson and exclusion of saddles on axes to characterize long-term behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: General two-species competition model form
rubrics_metrics.description: Write x' = M(x,y) x and y' = N(x,y) y where x,y ≥ 0 and M,N depend on both variables; nullclines are x=0, M(x,y)=0 and y=0, N(x,y)=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study qualitative properties of M and N (signs and partial derivatives) to deduce global phase-plane structure without specifying explicit functional forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition assumption: cross-partial signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Because species compete, an increase in one decreases the other's growth rate: ∂M/∂y < 0 and ∂N/∂x < 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This monotonicity implies nullclines µ = M^{-1}(0) and ν = N^{-1}(0) are graphs with well-defined orientation and enforces the four-type basic-region structure in the positive quadrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boundedness assumption for competition (existence of K)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists K > 0 such that M(x,y) < 0 and N(x,y) < 0 if x ≥ K or y ≥ K (if either population is very large, both populations decrease).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures solutions remain in a bounded region and that large populations have negative growth rates, enabling the use of invariant rectangles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-species growth assumption (constants a,b)
rubrics_metrics.description: In absence of the other species, each species has positive growth up to some threshold and negative beyond: there exist a,b > 0 with M(x,0) > 0 for x < a and M(x,0) < 0 for x > a; similarly N(0,y) > 0 for y < b and N(0,y) < 0 for y > b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This guarantees the nullclines µ and ν meet the axes at (a,0) and (0,b) respectively and gives biologically interpretable single-species carrying capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of µ and ν nullcline curves and basic regions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under assumptions (1) and (3), µ = M^{-1}(0) is the graph of a nonnegative function f:[0,a]→R with f^{-1}(0)=a; ν = N^{-1}(0) is the graph x = g(y) with g^{-1}(0)=b. The curves µ and ν and the axes partition the quadrant into basic regions of four sign-types (A,B,C,D) with monotone behavior in each region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nullcline graph properties and implicit function theorem allow classification of regions where x' and y' have definite signs; this precludes closed orbits within a basic region because x(t) and y(t) are monotone there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boundary-point proposition for basic regions (inward/outward)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any basic region R, the ordinary boundary points on µ and ν are either all inward (vector field points into R) or all outward (points out of R).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from transverse crossings of µ and ν and ensures each basic region closure is positively or negatively invariant, crucial for basin and limit analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: No closed orbits and ω-limit sets are equilibria in competition
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no closed orbits because closed orbits would have to lie in a basic region where x(t) and y(t) are monotone. Therefore every ω-limit set is an equilibrium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use monotonicity in basic regions and boundedness to conclude long-term behavior approaches equilibria; simplifies classification of eventual outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global convergence theorem for competitive systems
rubrics_metrics.description: For the competitive species system, the flow φ_t has the property that lim_{t→∞} φ_t(x,y) exists and is one of a finite number of equilibria for all x≥0,y≥0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence of partition into invariant basic regions, absence of closed orbits, and boundedness; biologically, two competing species tend to one of a finite set of limiting population outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability criterion at intersection vertex (slope/partial-derivative condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A vertex where µ and ν each have negative slope but µ is steeper (slope(µ) < slope(ν) < 0) is asymptotically stable. Equivalently, at an equilibrium with My<0 and Nx<0, if Mx<0 and Ny<0 then trace = x Mx + y Ny < 0 and determinant = x y (Mx Ny - My Nx) > 0, so eigenvalues have negative real parts (sink).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use slope comparison or partial-derivative sign conditions to conclude local asymptotic stability; drawing a small invariant rectangle around the equilibrium gives a geometric demonstration of sink behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of at least one sink and basin-dependence of outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be at least one asymptotically stable equilibrium (sink); which sink a solution tends to depends on initial condition and the stable manifolds partition basins of attraction. Small changes in initial conditions can cause jumps between basins (one species' extinction vs coexistence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ecological implication: perturbations (pesticide, immigration, fire) can move the system across basin boundaries causing drastic long-term changes; mathematically track stable curves and basin boundaries to predict outcomes.
